paras: You don't need to learn a second script for this: it's the same practice (gather attention, listen, respond, wait, return). Fifteen minutes or so is just a convenient appointment with yourself, not a therapeutic dose or a timetable your feelings have to follow. It's enough time to induce yourself (a few minutes), let the middle unfold at its own pace (five minutes of sitting in silence and listening is there when it's useful), and then bring yourself back out again (several minutes). You can interrupt the listening at any time to change direction.

paras: After practicing a few times with a recording, feel free to cut it down to the cues you still need. Then try practicing without playing it back. But keep using recordings if you enjoy them: being independent means you can guide yourself, not that you have to refuse help. (Note: the optional re-entry cue can shorten an induction you already know well.)

paras: When you come out of the process, consider whether there is anything you would like to nurture with more warmth, or protect, or direct in a way that moves it in the direction of truth and love and life. Perhaps there is something you would like to explore or build up. And what can you carry yourself now? If there is something you need to do, then make a plan with yourself to do that thing. Be concrete and say something like, "If _________ , then I will do ________ (one small action)." Then see how things are later on: how you are sleeping, relating and functioning, not only how impressive the session felt.
